column1: MARKET GAP ANALYSIS — Where Apollo can lead, not just react
Updated monthly. Gaps = sectors, geographies, products or capabilities underserved by current market participants. Apollo opportunity = where we can move first or differentiate.
SECTION A — IDENTIFIED MARKET GAPS & APOLLO OPPORTUNITY

Active Here?

column1:
Mid-market C&I (500kW–5MW demand)
Too big for rooftop solar, too small for bespoke long-term PPA
column4: Discovery Green / Ampli only — and very new
column5: Low — most traders ignore this tier
column8: Develop a standardised, flexible product specifically for mid-market. Shorter tenure (1–3 yr). Simple onboarding. Compete on ease, not just price.
column12: Ampli Energy is the only real mover here. Month-to-month product is disruptive. Apollo needs a response or a differentiated angle.

column1:
Agricultural sector
(Agri-processing, cold storage, irrigation, packhouses)
column3: Large — agri is 3rd largest electricity consumer sector in SA
column4: None visibly targeting agriculture
column8: Identify 5–10 large agri-processing or cold storage businesses as pilot targets. Build an agri-specific value proposition around seasonal demand flexibility.
column12: No publicised agriculture PPAs found across any competitor. Clean green energy + water/carbon story resonates strongly in agri export sector.

column1:
Data centres & hyperscaler facilities
(24/7 baseload, high volume, sustainability-driven)
column3: Fast-growing — SA attracting major hyperscaler investment
column4: NOA Group (stated target) — no confirmed deals yet
column8: Approach SA data centre operators and hyperscaler site selectors now. Develop a blended wind/solar/BESS product for 24/7 coverage. This customer class will need 100MW+ supply.
column12: NOA named data centres as target sector. No one has signed a deal. First mover wins credibility. SA's data centre market is accelerating.

column1:
Short-tenure PPAs (1–5 year)
Flexible contracts aligned to business planning cycles
column4: Enpower only (pioneered 5-yr with Sappi)
column5: Low — one deal, not a product strategy
column8: Build a formal short-tenure PPA product with standard terms, clear pricing methodology and fast turnaround. As SAWEM approaches, buyers will demand more flexibility.
column12: Enpower called 5-yr PPA a 'game-changer' and 'market-first.' Apollo should build on this signal and develop a competing flexible product before others do.

column1:
Municipal supply agreements (municipalities as buyers)
Not just as grid owners, but as energy customers
column4: BluEnergy only (Feb 2026 licence, not yet trading)
column5: Very low — only BluEnergy positioned here
column8: Identify 3–5 progressive municipalities open to buying renewable energy for their own infrastructure. Use revenue-neutral model. Build relationships before BluEnergy operationalises.
column12: BluEnergy has Cigicell infrastructure advantage in 95+ municipalities. Apollo needs a differentiated angle — possibly local content, local IPPs, or community benefit.

column1:
Cross-border / SAPP trading
(Import/Export licence for SADC energy flows)
column4: GreenCo (focused), Enpower (licence granted Jul 2025), NTCSA
column5: Low among private traders — GreenCo is the only active cross-border operator
column8: Assess feasibility of applying for an Import/Export licence. Would make Apollo one of only 3 private traders with cross-border capability. Particularly valuable as SA grid opens.
column12: Only 2 private companies hold I/E licences. Cross-border is structurally important as SA integrates into SAPP. Early positioning has regulatory and commercial value.

column1:
BESS-backed firm power product
Battery storage enabling 24/7 or peak-guarantee supply
column4: NOA (adding BESS to Khauta complex), Etana (blended portfolio)
column5: Low — few traders have a BESS-specific product
column8: Develop a storage-backed 'firm power' product in partnership with a BESS IPP. Positions Apollo as solving the intermittency problem — a key objection from industrial buyers.
column12: The single biggest objection from large industrial buyers is 'what happens at night / when wind drops.' A BESS-backed firm product directly addresses this.

column1:
Retail / FMCG / cold chain sector
(Food manufacturing, retail distribution, cold storage)
column4: EXSA (Woolworths, Siqalo Foods) — early mover
column5: Low — EXSA has a few deals but not a sector strategy
column8: Develop targeted outreach to SA's top 20 food manufacturers and cold chain operators. Multi-site, multi-province deals align well with Apollo's aggregation capability.
column12: EXSA's Woolworths deal signals this sector is opening up. Multi-site retail and FMCG is a natural fit for a trader who can manage complex wheeling across provinces.

column1:
SME / multi-tenant commercial property
(Smaller offices, light industrial parks, mixed-use)
column3: Very large — SMEs = 98% of SA businesses
column4: Ampli Energy (Discovery Green + Sasol) — month-to-month
column5: Low — only Ampli targeting this; product very new
column8: Consider a co-branded or white-label product for commercial property managers to offer tenants. Leverages existing Reunert Group relationships.
column12: Ampli's month-to-month cashback model is disruptive for SMEs. Apollo's differentiation could be through property management relationships via Reunert.

column1:
Hospitals, healthcare & education
(Uninterrupted supply critical; ESG reporting growing)
column4: None identified targeting healthcare or education
column8: Approach private hospital groups (Mediclinic, Netcare, Life Healthcare) and large private universities. Reliable supply + ESG credentials are key buying criteria here.
column12: Mediclinic is a Remgro company (EXSA parent). Apollo could target Netcare, Life Healthcare. Education sector (universities, private schools) has large campuses and ESG mandates.

column4: Financial credibility and balance sheet strength. Use this to offer payment guarantees and longer-tenor products that smaller traders cannot match.
Apollo has no IPP parent pushing its own projects. This is a genuine differentiator — Apollo can source from any IPP, giving customers a truly independent, best-of-market portfolio.
Smaller team than IPP-linked traders means faster deal execution. Market this aggressively. 'We can be in market faster than anyone else.'
Pick 1–2 underserved sectors (e.g. agriculture, data centres) and go deep. Build case studies, sector-specific pricing, dedicated relationships. Become known as the expert in those sectors.
Build the best 1–5 year product in the market. As SAWEM approaches, this becomes the market-standard contract. Apollo should own this space.
Most buyers still do not understand how trading works. Apollo's comms strategy should educate the market. The brand that teaches the market often wins the market.
